key_insight: A decision model that acts poorly can still teach effectively by judging actions after their consequences are visible.
engineering_relevance: Use decision models as retrospective action evaluators to train agent policies, rather than selecting them solely by their own task success.
method: Compare three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and judges on ALFWorld.
Evaluate actions using full trajectories and ask whether each action helped, rather than whether the task will succeed.
Use JEV as a teacher for a Qwen2.5-1.5B policy on ALFWorld and WebShop.
evidence_signal: JEV teaching improved success over GRPO from 72.8% to 82.9% on ALFWorld and from 56.8% to 71.4% on WebShop.
watch_item: Teaching results cover one teacher and two benchmarks; full-trajectory judgments require completed episodes and do not establish real-time decision quality.
paper_title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
